report.summary: The only failing test, test_book_can_be_updated, fails because its own expected value is wrong: it sends year=2001 on the PUT but asserts the stored year is 2002. The application stores and returns the year it was sent, so the fix belongs in the test, not the app. Change the expected year to 2001 (or send 2002) in tests/api/test_books_api.py:23-27.

causes.title: Test expects year 2002 after updating to 2001
causes.explanation: test_book_can_be_updated calls api.update_book with year=2001, then asserts that GET returns year 2002. The app's PUT handler writes the submitted year unchanged (UPDATE books SET ... year = ? with book.year), and GET returns that stored value, so the correct result is 2001. The assertion mismatch is a typo or a stale expectation in the test. Nothing in the app adds one to the year.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:215-216: UPDATE books SET title = ?, author = ?, year = ? WHERE id = ?, (book.title, book.author, book.year, book_id)
The PUT response (status 200 assertion at line 25) passed, so the update request was accepted and the stored value is what the GET returned, 2001.
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 27, change "year": 2002 to "year": 2001 so it matches the year sent on line 23.
